area: 2D camera: implementing the measured OG behavior (ledger b-6) in the Phaser 3 / render-only-scene architecture

item_verdicts.title: Canon camera smoothing (lerp, deadzone, look-ahead) is a fidelity DEFECT here — the OG is a pure position-lock with edge-snap
item_verdicts.why: Both sources check out: the Game Developer reprint of Keren's 'Scroll Back' defines position-locking ('Camera is locked to the player's position'), camera-window ('Push camera position as the player hits the window edge'), dual-forward-focus and edge-snapping ('Set a hard edge for camera positioning'), and ledger b-6 (COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md §b-6) says verbatim what is quoted: pin at screen x≈1072–1082 @1080 (≈56%), scroll at exactly the character's world speed (587 px/s @1080 = 313 stage px/s), hard clamp at zone edges. The anti-smoothing / anti-look-ahead half survives. The 'no camera window' half is REFUTED by a source the research never opened: docs/research/fidelity/SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.4 (CONTRACT-SRC, v0.717 payload, decompiled 2026-07-25) carries the row `camera dead-band | screen x 350–450` in the original's own 800×480 world space. That is Keren's camera-window, taken from the game's own code, and it OUTRANKS the video row per §0 tagging ('MEASURED ... until a CONTRACT-SRC value replaces it'). It also explains b-6 rather than conflicting with it: 450 world px through the repo's own transform (stage = 32 + 1.2·worldX, src/core/viewport.ts) is stage 572 = 55.86% of 1024 = 1072.5 px @1080 — the exact bottom of the measured 1072–1082 band.
item_verdicts.correction: The OG camera is Keren's CAMERA-WINDOW + EDGE-SNAPPING, not position-locking. Correct spec line: camera window of world x [350, 450] (CONTRACT-SRC, SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.4), zero smoothing, zero look-ahead, hard clamp at zone edges (b-6). What stays rejected: lerp<1 smoothing and look-ahead. What is now ADOPTED, not rejected: the deadzone/camera-window itself.

item_verdicts.title: Exact Phaser 3 mapping exists — startFollow(player, false, 1, 1) + followOffset.x = +(0.56−0.5)·width + setBounds — but ADAPT to a core-owned scroll formula instead
item_verdicts.why: Every Phaser semantic checks out verbatim against the official API docs (docs.phaser.io/api-documentation/class/cameras-scene2d-camera): startFollow defaults lerpX/lerpY = 1 and 'A value of 1 means the camera will instantly snap to the target coordinates'; followOffset values 'are subtracted from the Camera targets position'; and the Discourse thread's clamp claim is real (samme: 'That part is normal, as the camera can't leave the bounds even while following a target'). The architecture argument also checks out in the repo: src/core/viewport.ts really does own worldToStage/stageToWorld/VIEW, src/game/CLAUDE.md line 1 is 'Phaser scenes, render-only', and DuelScene.ts imports stageToWorld/VIEW/worldToStage and planPose — so core-owned scrollX is right. TWO defects in the numbers. (1) Wrong model: the formula is a pure lock; the payload says camera-window (SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.4 dead-band 350–450), so scroll is an edge-push, not scrollX = playerX − anchor. (2) Bad arithmetic even for its own model: '1077/1920 ≈ 56.1% of 800 = 448.5' silently assumes the world spans the whole stage, but the repo's transcribed original transform is stage = 32 + 1.2·worldX with 32 px pillarbox bars (viewport.ts, SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.10). 1077 px @1080 → stage 574.4 → world 452.0, not 448 — a 4 world-px error, larger than b-6's own ±2 world-px band.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace the single-anchor formula with the source-measured window. Core: scrollX = clamp(scrollX_prev, playerX − CAM_WINDOW_RIGHT, playerX − CAM_WINDOW_LEFT) then clamp(0, zoneWidth − WORLD_WIDTH), with CAM_WINDOW_LEFT = 350 and CAM_WINDOW_RIGHT = 450 world px (CONTRACT-SRC, SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.4). Phaser cross-check becomes startFollow(player, false, 1, 1) + setDeadzone(100, viewHeight) + setBounds — no followOffset. Delete the 448 figure entirely; if anyone re-derives an anchor from video it is 452 world px (stageToWorld of 1077 @1080), because the transform carries a +32 px pillarbox offset.

item_verdicts.title: Duels are fixed-camera and the repo already does exactly that — no camera work belongs in DuelScene
item_verdicts.why: The repo half is CONFIRMED at the pixels: `grep -rn -i camera src/` returns exactly ONE hit repo-wide — src/config/anim.ts:21, the 'fixed-camera window t=465.0–466.3' comment — and grep for camera in src/game/DuelScene.ts exits 1 (zero matches); DuelScene renders via planPose(playerParts, FIGHTER_SHAPES, {...}, VIEW) with the static VIEW transform. (Note the research's own dead_ends line is wrong here: progression.ts's 'Rebirth Scroll' does not contain the word camera; the grep yields one mention, not two.) The JUSTIFICATION is over-claimed. §S24-A step 2 states strokes hang world-anchored and 'drift exactly with camera pans', and the §S24-H Verify-pass block (2026-08-12, wf_56ff205f-341) states outright: 'The dojo camera is NOT locked past f0094 (~6 px pan by f0096, ~27 px by f0098) — fleet tick values after f0094 are contaminated.' Also false: 'all movement measured directly in screen px (no camera-subtraction step needed)' — §S24-C quotes the VS-duel legs as '+400/+198/−107/−106/+326 px world' and flags the mob legs as 'camera-checked'. And the payload mine found ONE camera dead-band with no duel exemption recorded.
item_verdicts.correction: Keep the conclusion (no camera code in DuelScene today) but restate the reason: the duel camera is UNMEASURED/CONTESTED, not 'explicitly fixed'. Evidence against a blanket fixed-camera duel rule: §S24-H (2026-08-12) 'The dojo camera is NOT locked past f0094 (~6 px pan by f0096, ~27 px by f0098)' and §S24-A 'drifts exactly with camera pans'. anim.ts's 'fixed-camera window t=465.0–466.3' is a 1.3 s hand-picked measurement window, not a scene-wide camera verdict. So: no camera work in DuelScene until the duel camera is measured, and the standing rule should read 'unproven — do not add follow, do not assert fixed either'.

item_verdicts.title: Never use Phaser setDeadzone — the OG has no camera window
item_verdicts.why: Killed by the repo's own authoritative source file. docs/research/fidelity/SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.4 (header: '§3 Duels constants (CONTRACT-SRC, v0.717 unless noted)... World space is 800 × 480') lists `camera dead-band | screen x 350–450`. The original game literally has a camera window, read out of its decompiled code, in the same build (v0.717) the video measurements came from — and CONTRACT-SRC outranks video-MEASURED per §0. The item's supporting argument is also inverted: the 1072–1082 @1080 band is not 'noise proving a hard lock', it IS the window edge — 450 world px → stage 32+1.2·450 = 572 → 55.86% of 1024 → 1072.5 px @1080, the exact low end of the measured band. Phaser's setDeadzone ('a rectangular region where, if the target is present, the camera will not scroll', docs verified) is the correct semantic match for the OG, not a forbidden affordance.

item_verdicts.title: Left-travel camera anchor is UNMEASURED — measure before implementing bidirectional scroll
item_verdicts.why: The premise is true as far as the ledger goes — b-6 does scope its pin to 'when running right', and no other ledger row gives a leftward anchor. But 'cannot be inferred' is wrong: SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md §3.4's CONTRACT-SRC dead-band 350–450 world px is symmetric about the world centre (400), so leftward travel pins at the band's LEFT edge, 350 world px = stage 452 = 44.14% = 847 px @1080 — the mirrored ~44% the item lists as one of three unknowable options, and it rules out dual-forward focus (a directional flip would need two bands or an animated one; the payload has a single static pair). The citation is also loose: §S24-C's beach −178/−271 px legs are IN-COMBAT retreat/approach legs, not zone-traversal leftward running, so they are not the measurement window the item points at.
item_verdicts.correction: Downgrade MEASURE_FIRST → cross-check. The leftward anchor is ANSWERED by CONTRACT-SRC: dead-band world x [350, 450] is symmetric about the 400 centre ⇒ running left pins at 350 world px (stage 452 = 44.1% = ~847 px @1080), instant edge-push on reversal, no dual-forward focus. A video pass over a leftward zone-travel window is now the §5 tier-3 confirmation step (predict 847 px @1080), not a prerequisite for implementing. And drop the §S24-C beach −178/−271 cite — those are in-combat legs, not zone running.

item_verdicts.title: Parallax layers ride the camera: boulder layer at 0.73×, plus a fixed screen overlay — implement as per-layer scroll factors in config
item_verdicts.why: Ledger §S24-G trap 9 says exactly this, verbatim: 'A28 forest: the bottom-left mushroom cluster is a FIXED screen overlay (dx=0, corr 1.00 — a fake "static camera" anchor); the boulder layer parallaxes at 0.73×. Anchor on hanging strokes or actor-plane props.' Nothing in the §00b corrections table (which touches f-8/f-10, f-9, e-7, a-6 only) or in the §S24-H Verify-pass corrections block (2026-08-12: §S24-B band, A28 S3 cinematic, §S24-C point-blank, §S24-E dash model, §S24-D run band) overturns trap 9. The measurement-tooling warning ('never anchor camera-motion measurement on a layer whose factor isn't 1.0') is a fair restatement of trap 9's own 'anchor on hanging strokes or actor-plane props'. Two scope notes, neither fatal: 0.73× is video-MEASURED from one zone (A28 forest), so per SOURCE_CONSTANTS §0 tagging it is MEASURED-tier and one zone's factor, not a global; and the Phaser scrollFactor semantics cited are consistent with the API docs I fetched.

overall_note:
Sources are clean — I spot-checked four URLs and all four say what the research attributes to them (Phaser Camera API docs confirm lerp 1 = 'instantly snap' and followOffset 'subtracted from the Camera targets position' and the deadzone 'will not scroll' semantics; the Game Developer 'Scroll Back' reprint defines position-locking, camera-window, dual-forward-focus and edge-snapping; the GDC Vault entry is live and is Itay Keren, 2015, behind a membership wall; the Discourse thread's setBounds+follow clamp is confirmed by samme). The ledger rows (b-6, §S24-C, §S24-G trap 9) all say what is claimed, and neither §00b nor the new §S24-H Verify-pass corrections block (2026-08-12) touches them.

The research's real failure is a MISSED SOURCE, and it takes down its two REJECT items. Its dead_ends section asserts 'No source of any kind was found describing the original SHS: Duels Flash camera implementation (searching would have been redundant: the repo's P0 experiment already established the payload needs the dead Player.IO backend)'. That conflates 'no playable build' with 'no source'. The payload was DECRYPTED, DECOMPILED AND MINED on 2026-07-25 — docs/research/fidelity/SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md, 189 constants, 152 CONFIRMED / 37 CORRECTED / 0 REFUTED, build v0.717, the same build the videos came from — and §3.4 contains `camera dead-band | screen x 350–450`. So the OG HAS a camera window, the single technique the research spent two items forbidding. The arithmetic seals it: 450 world px through the repo's own transcribed transform (stage = 32 + 1.2·worldX, src/core/viewport.ts + SOURCE_CONSTANTS §3.10) = stage 572 = 55.86% of 1024 = 1072.5 px @1080, landing exactly on the low edge of b-6's measured 1072–1082 pin band. The video measurement and the source constant are the same fact; the research read the window edge as a hard lock. Two second-order consequences: the proposed CAMERA_ANCHOR_X = 448 is both the wrong MODEL and wrong ARITHMETIC (dropping the 32 px pillarbox gives 452, not 448), and the 'unmeasurable' left anchor falls straight out of the symmetric band at 350 world px (44.1%, ~847 px @1080).

Repo checks all passed as stated: `grep -rn -i camera src/` returns exactly one hit (src/config/anim.ts:21 comment) — zero executable camera code anywhere, DuelScene.ts has no camera reference and draws via planPose(..., VIEW); src/config/display.ts holds GAME_WIDTH 1024 / GAME_HEIGHT 576 / WORLD_WIDTH 800 / WORLD_HEIGHT 480 as claimed. Standing lesson for the next research pass in this repo: SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md is a mandatory read before declaring any OG mechanic 'video-only ground truth'.
